error.message: Antigravity ResultPackage missing: root agent idle; waiting up to 5s for 2 background task(s)

instructions: Continue TASK-136 r2 implementation from the clean failed base.
Implement REPAIR-of-REMEDIATION review authoring using canonical repair lineage and bind prior_finding_id to the exact repaired remediation finding.
Add production-topology regressions in tests/test_authoring_ingress.py with test names containing repair_review so the focused selector executes real tests.
Complete the implementation, commit the authorized changes, and return a structural ResultPackage.

acceptance.condition: SUBMIT_REVIEW detects canonical repair.json and reconstructs the exact immutable REPAIR lineage instead of treating the repaired RUN as an ordinary primary RUN.

A successful REPAIR of REMEDIATION accepts a DELTA REVIEW only when prior_finding_id equals the exact finding_id of the canonical REMEDIATION being repaired and validates that review against the reconstructed prior REVIEW. A different finding that merely exists in the same prior REVIEW is rejected.
Wrong, absent, stale, malformed, ambiguous, or discontinuous REPAIR lineage and wrong review mode/finding fail closed without creating a review-decision ref.
A successful REPAIR before any semantic finding retains PRIMARY review semantics, while existing non-REPAIR PRIMARY and REMEDIATION review authoring remain compatible.
Successful REPAIR ResultPackage validation uses the correct REPAIR root/package semantics and remains consistent with Publisher's independent lineage validation.

New focused repair_review regressions are present and actually execute, the full authoring-ingress suite passes, git diff checking passes, RESULT has no unresolved items, and implementation mutation remains within authoring_ingress.py and its focused tests.

assumptions: Canonical main at revision-2 authoring is 68f3737a87ac07212609521e8d41ed10fcb2bc8f.
RUN-135-004 canonical review candidate is d4c822d64e43713995134d89c5b663f7d2a3390f and its artifacts contain .ai/transport/repair.json binding REPAIR-135-003-001 to failed RUN-135-003.
Publisher's existing REPAIR-lineage semantics are authoritative and already require DELTA REVIEW for REPAIR of REMEDIATION and PRIMARY REVIEW only for REPAIR before any semantic finding.

The dirty local WIP left by failed RUN-136-001 is not canonical lifecycle state and must not be treated as an admitted candidate, predecessor, or source of authority. It may be consulted only as implementation reference after the Executor starts from a clean canonical base.
No semantic changes are required to TASK-135, RUN-135-004, REVIEW-135-001, REVIEW-135-002, either remediation, or REPAIR authorization.

hard: SUBMIT_REVIEW must inspect canonical successful artifacts for optional .ai/transport/repair.json. Its absence preserves existing PRIMARY/REMEDIATION behavior byte-for-byte.

When repair.json is present, Authoring Ingress must reconstruct the canonical REPAIR lineage from immutable remote evidence, including the exact failed RUN, canonical FAILURE artifacts, current REPAIR authorization, repaired candidate, TASK identity/revision, semantic predecessor, prior REVIEW, and—when that predecessor is a REMEDIATION—the exact remediation finding_id.

Reuse the same semantic validation rules as Publisher rather than introducing a weaker parallel interpretation. If shared helpers are reused, Authoring Ingress must map their failures to AuthoringIngressError without weakening fail-closed behavior.

For REPAIR of a REMEDIATION candidate, SUBMIT_REVIEW must require mode DELTA and prior_finding_id must equal the exact finding_id of the canonical REMEDIATION being repaired. It is not sufficient that prior_finding_id merely names any finding that exists in the prior REVIEW. The submitted REVIEW must then validate against that reconstructed prior REVIEW.

The exact repaired remediation finding must be derived from canonical predecessor REMEDIATION lineage, not inferred from review ordering, set membership, candidate changed files, local state, or caller-supplied review metadata.
For REPAIR before any semantic finding, existing PRIMARY REVIEW semantics remain valid and DELTA review must not be invented.
Missing, malformed, stale, ambiguous, mismatched, or semantically discontinuous repair lineage must fail closed before creating refs/heads/aios/review-decision/<RUN>.

The successful REPAIR ResultPackage must be validated with REPAIR package semantics from the correct repair root, not accidentally reinterpreted as an ordinary PRIMARY ResultPackage merely because run.json is plain.
The implementation must not mutate candidate refs, artifact refs, repair refs, failure refs, main, or historical metadata. SUBMIT_REVIEW remains metadata-only.
REVIEW idempotency/conflict behavior and all existing PRIMARY and direct REMEDIATION review-authoring behavior remain compatible.

New production-topology regressions must be added to tests/test_authoring_ingress.py for at least: successful REPAIR-of-REMEDIATION DELTA PASS; a prior REVIEW with two findings where the wrong existing finding_id is rejected; missing prior_finding_id; PRIMARY review incorrectly used for repaired remediation; malformed or missing repair lineage; repaired PRIMARY still accepting PRIMARY review; and no review-decision ref on every rejected case.

Focused verification must execute at least one newly added REPAIR-review regression; a command that deselects all tests is not evidence. Test names for the new group must contain repair_review so the required focused selector is deterministic.

RUN-136-001 local WIP may be read as a hint only after the workspace has been reset to canonical main. The Executor must produce a fresh committed candidate and structural ResultPackage through normal TASK-136 r2 PRIMARY execution.

task.goal: Make Brain Authoring Ingress canonicalize the correct DELTA REVIEW for a successful REPAIR of a REMEDIATION candidate by reconstructing and validating the immutable REPAIR lineage from canonical artifacts, using the same semantic rules already enforced by Publisher and binding the REVIEW to the exact repaired remediation finding.
non_goals: Change TASK-135 implementation semantics or acceptance criteria.
Change REPAIR execution, repair-wakeup, remediation execution, correction frontier, or publication behavior.
Relax Publisher's requirement that REPAIR of REMEDIATION receives a DELTA REVIEW.
Convert RUN-135-004 into a REMEDIATION-shaped run.json or rewrite historical artifacts.
Add a generic lifecycle router, planner, fallback, retry, or automatic review generation.
Fix the separate self-hosted REPAIR GITHUB_ACTOR provenance bug in this task.
Treat RUN-136-001 dirty WIP as a valid candidate or bypass normal PRIMARY lifecycle.
Push or publish from the coding Executor.
task.problem: TASK-135 RUN-135-004 is a successful FINALIZE_CANDIDATE REPAIR of failed REMEDIATION RUN-135-003. Its successful artifacts contain plain .ai/transport/run.json and .ai/transport/result.json plus .ai/transport/repair.json. Publisher correctly detects repair.json, reconstructs the failed predecessor lineage, determines that the repaired candidate belongs to FINDING-135-002, and requires a DELTA REVIEW whose prior_finding_id matches that semantic finding. Brain Authoring Ingress SUBMIT_REVIEW, however, currently reads only run.json and result.json and cannot reconstruct that lineage. TASK-136 r1's first PRIMARY attempt, RUN-136-001, failed before producing a ResultPackage and left only an uncommitted local WIP. Audit of that WIP found two additional requirements that must be explicit in the canonical contract: the DELTA review must bind to the exact remediation finding rather than merely any finding in the prior review, and production-topology regression tests must actually be added and executed.
